cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup. I taught you to look for value, not labels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's proper coffee in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to keep a reserve. Taste this and we might save the real stuff for guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My breakfast isn't your budgeting exercise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally valuing your time. One sip, and I'll buy you a croissant if it's awful. My cup stays empty until you give your verdict.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 value lesson asks pupil first taste; A3 credits B2 available stock as learned reserve; A5 grades B4 refusal as valuation then offers compensation while keeping own cup empty.

relationship.evidence: B4 protects its actual breakfast and refuses to be an unpriced test subject.

heightening.evidence: A5 reduces the demanded trial and pays for failure, but still waits for B verdict.

specificity.evidence: A1 cheap substitute and B2 real supply make testing optional and self-serving.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 empty-cup statement is a concrete commitment clarifying who relies on the result first.
